relations.definition: To take someone into custody, typically by a law enforcement agency.
relations.embedding_query_text: arrested: To take someone into custody, typically by a law enforcement agency.

chosen_property.label: arrested
chosen_property.definition: To take someone into custody, typically by a law enforcement agency.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: legislationLegalForce
candidates.comment: A legal force status relation between a piece of legislation and its current state of being in force. Also called: force status, legal validity, in effect status. Examples: "New Act legislationLegalForce InForce", "Old Regulation legislationLegalForce NotInForce", "Partial Amendment legislationLegalForce PartiallyInForce".

candidates.label: bookingAgent
candidates.comment: An organization or person acting as a broker or booking agent for a reservation. Also called: reservation agent, travel agent, broker. Examples: "Reservation 'Hotel Stay' bookingAgent 'Booking.com'", "Reservation 'Flight' bookingAgent 'Travel Agency X'."

candidates.label: drug
candidates.comment: A drug relation between a medical entity (such as a drug class, condition, patient, or therapeutic procedure) and a specific drug or medicine. Also called "medication used", "prescribed drug", "contains drug". Examples: "Medical condition 'Hypertension' drug 'Lisinopril'", "Therapeutic procedure 'Chemotherapy' drug 'Paclitaxel'", "Drug class 'Statins' drug 'Atorvastatin'".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: referee
candidates.comment: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: servicePhone
candidates.comment: The contact point, typically a phone number, used to access a service. Also called service contact number, service hotline, phone access. Examples: `Customer Support Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 1-800-XXX-XXXX`, `Emergency Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 911`, `Booking Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: Local Booking Line`. Distinct from `telephone`, which is a general phone number for an entity.

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

relations.definition: To provide information or news about something, often in an official capacity.
relations.embedding_query_text: reported: To provide information or news about something, often in an official capacity.

chosen_property.label: reported
chosen_property.definition: To provide information or news about something, often in an official capacity.

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: schoolClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.

relations.definition: To provide an opinion or statement about something, often in a public or official context.
relations.embedding_query_text: commented on: To provide an opinion or statement about something, often in a public or official context.

chosen_property.label: comment
chosen_property.justification: The 'comment' property from schema.org fits the relation.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: comment
candidates.comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.

candidates.label: commentText
candidates.comment: A textual content relation for user comments, providing the actual text of the comment. Also called "comment content", "message text", "user feedback text". Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: discussionUrl
candidates.comment: A discussion URL relation between a creative work and the URL of the page where its comments are located. Also called "comments page link", "forum link", "feedback URL". Examples: "Movie 'Inception' discussionUrl 'example.com/inception/comments'", "Article 'Quantum Physics' discussionUrl 'forum.example.org/quantum'", "Book '1984' discussionUrl 'goodreads.com/1984/discussion'". Distinct from discusses, which is the creative work that a user comment is about.

relations.definition: To see or experience something, often in a role as an observer or bystander.
relations.embedding_query_text: witnessed: To see or experience something, often in a role as an observer or bystander.

chosen_property.label: witnessed
chosen_property.definition: To see or experience something, often in a role as an observer or bystander.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: sensoryRequirement
candidates.comment: A description, defined term, or URL detailing the sensory abilities (e.g., hearing, vision) required for a job. Also called sensory abilities, perceptual requirements, job sensory needs. Examples: `Call Center Job` sensoryRequirement `"Excellent hearing"`, `Graphic Designer Role` sensoryRequirement `"Normal color vision"`, `Pilot Position` sensoryRequirement `URL to FAA medical standards`. Distinct from `physicalRequirement`, which is about physical capabilities.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

relations.definition: The place where something is situated or occurs.
relations.embedding_query_text: location of: The place where something is situated or occurs.

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property from schema.org fits the relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: latitude
candidates.comment: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.

relations.definition: To be a component or subset of something larger.
relations.embedding_query_text: part of: To be a component or subset of something larger.

chosen_property.label: subEvent
chosen_property.justification: The 'subEvent' property from schema.org fits the relation.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

relations.definition: To come before something in time or sequence.
relations.embedding_query_text: preceded: To come before something in time or sequence.

chosen_property.label: preceded
chosen_property.definition: To come before something in time or sequence.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

relations.definition: Relating to or concerning something, often in a descriptive or explanatory sense.
relations.embedding_query_text: about: Relating to or concerning something, often in a descriptive or explanatory sense.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property from schema.org fits the relation.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: keywords
candidates.comment: A descriptive tagging relation between an item (creative work, event, organization, place, product) and the terms or phrases used to categorize or describe it. Also called tags, descriptors, categories, labels, search terms. Examples: A blog post has keywords 'AI, machine learning, future tech'. An event has keywords 'music festival, summer, outdoor'. A product has keywords 'eco-friendly, sustainable, organic'. Distinct from about, which describes the primary topic, not just descriptive tags.

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: nerve
candidates.comment: A nerve providing innervation to a muscle. Also called innervated by, muscle innervation, nerve supply. Examples: "Biceps Brachii nerve 'Musculocutaneous nerve'", "Triceps Brachii nerve 'Radial nerve'", "Diaphragm nerve 'Phrenic nerve'". Distinct from nerveMotor, which describes the muscle controlled by a nerve.

candidates.label: overdosage
candidates.comment: Information related to drug overdose, including signs, symptoms, treatments, and emergency contact details. Also called overdose information, toxicity details, emergency overdose guidance. Examples: "Drug X overdosage 'Symptoms include nausea and dizziness. Contact poison control immediately.'", "Medication Y overdosage 'Administer activated charcoal. Seek urgent medical attention.'", "Supplement Z overdosage 'May cause liver damage in high doses.'". Distinct from sideEffect, which describes adverse effects at normal doses.

instances: an off-duty police officer -> the suspect

chosen_property.label: apprehended
chosen_property.definition: To take someone into custody, typically by a law enforcement agency.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: paymentAccepted
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the types of payment methods accepted by a local business. Also called accepted payment methods, payment options, forms of payment. Examples: A restaurant accepts 'Cash'. A store accepts 'Credit Card'. An online shop accepts 'Cryptocurrency'.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: dateIssued
candidates.comment: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".

candidates.label: currenciesAccepted
candidates.comment: A payment method relation between a local business and the currencies it accepts. Also called: accepted currency, payment currency, currency options. Examples: "Coffee Shop" currencies accepted "USD, EUR", "Online Store" currencies accepted "USD, BTC", "Local Market" currencies accepted "Ithaca HOUR". Distinct from currency, which specifies the currency of a monetary amount.

candidates.label: inStoreReturnsOffered
candidates.comment: An in-store returns offering relation for a merchant return policy, indicating whether returns can be made in a physical store. Also called in-store returns available, physical store returns, returns accepted in store. Examples: "A merchant return policy has in-store returns offered.", "The policy indicates if in-store returns are offered.", "This return policy allows in-store returns."

candidates.label: ticketedSeat
candidates.comment: An association between a ticket and the specific seat it grants access to. Also called "assigned seat", "seat number", "ticket seat allocation". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketedSeat Row A, Seat 12", "The flight ticket's ticketedSeat is 23F", "This ticket is for a specific ticketedSeat."

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

instances: a young man with a small suitcase -> the suspect

chosen_property.label: hit
chosen_property.definition: To strike or come into contact with something or someone.

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: track
candidates.comment: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: audio
candidates.comment: An embedded audio object associated with a creative work. Also called: audio file, sound recording, soundtrack. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Podcast Episode' audio 'AudioObject of Episode'", "CreativeWork 'Movie' audio 'Soundtrack Clip'", "CreativeWork 'Webpage' audio 'Background Music'."

candidates.label: catalogNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a music release and its unique catalog number. Also called "release ID", "record label number", "product number". Examples: "Album release catalogNumber 'ABC-123'", "Single release catalogNumber 'XYZ-456'".

candidates.label: musicReleaseFormat
candidates.comment: The format of a music release, indicating the type of recording media. Also called release format, media type, recording format. Examples: "Album X musicReleaseFormat 'CDFormat'", "Single Y musicReleaseFormat 'DigitalAudioTapeFormat'", "LP Z musicReleaseFormat 'VinylFormat'".

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

instances: a waiter from a nearby restaurant -> the suspect

chosen_property.label: restrained
chosen_property.definition: To hold or keep someone or something under control.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: antagonist
candidates.comment: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."

candidates.label: suitableForDiet
candidates.comment: An indication of a dietary restriction or guideline for which a recipe or menu item is appropriate. Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: constraintProperty
candidates.comment: A definitional relation for a constraint node, indicating a property used as a constraint. Also called "constraining property", "restricted by property", "property constraint". Examples: "Statistical variable constraint node constraintProperty 'schema:age'", "Data filter constraintProperty 'dc:gender'".

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: regionDrained
candidates.comment: A region drained relation between a lymphatic vessel or vein and the anatomical structure or system from which it removes fluid. Also called drains region, supplies drainage to. Examples: "The femoral vein drains region 'the leg'.", "A lymphatic vessel drains region 'the arm'.", "The hepatic portal vein drains region 'the digestive tract'."

candidates.label: petsAllowed
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating whether pets are permitted in an accommodation or lodging business. Also called pet-friendly, animal policy, pet access. Examples: A hotel has 'pets allowed' set to 'true'. An apartment complex has 'pets allowed' set to 'Small dogs only'. A lodging business has 'pets allowed' set to 'false'.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

chosen_property.label: carriedOut
chosen_property.definition: To perform or execute an action or event.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: itemShipped
candidates.comment: A shipment content relation between a parcel delivery and the product(s) being transported. Also called shipped product, contents of shipment, parcel contents, delivered item. Examples: A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'a book'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'clothing items'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'electronic device'.

candidates.label: deliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A logistical approach relation between an order, receive, send, or track action and the method used for delivery. Also called: shipping method, delivery mode, transport method. Examples: "Online Purchase" delivery method "Standard Shipping", "Document Send" delivery method "Email", "Package Tracking" delivery method "Courier Service".

candidates.label: handlingTime
candidates.comment: A processing time relation between a shipping service or delivery time and the duration required for order fulfillment. Also called processing duration, preparation time, fulfillment time, lead time. Examples: "A shipping service has a handling time of 2 days.", "The delivery time includes a handling time of 1-3 business days.", "Order processing has a handling time of 24 hours."

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: providesBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A broadcast service provision relation between a broadcast channel and the specific broadcast service it offers. Also called channel offers, service on channel, carries service. Examples: "Channel 5 provides broadcast service 'News at 6'.", "BBC One provides broadcast service 'EastEnders'.", "A radio channel provides broadcast service 'Morning Show'."

candidates.label: serviceOutput
candidates.comment: The tangible item or product that is generated or delivered as a result of a service. Also called service product, service deliverable, output of service. Examples: `Passport Application Service` serviceOutput `Passport`, `Permit Application Service` serviceOutput `Building Permit`, `Printing Service` serviceOutput `Printed Documents`.

candidates.label: availableDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method available for an offer. Also called: shipping option, delivery option, fulfillment method. Examples: "Offer 'Product Z' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Shipping'", "Offer 'Food' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Pickup'."
